#833. Taylor Frankie Paul Shares Update on Sex Life After Cheating Scandal

Taylor Frankie Paul revealed she’s been celibate for nearly one year: “If you’re familiar with how I am, you know it’s the opposite of what I would have normally done.”

Taylor Frankie Paul is spilling secrets about her sex life.

Following The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star’s bombshell admission that she cheated on her former fiancé Doug Mason with ex Dakota Mortensen, she revealed she’s been celibate for nearly one year.

“The fact that I remained single and celibate during the 10 loneliest months of life has me shocked,” Paul wrote over a video of herself dancing on Instagram Nov. 8, “but progress I guess.”

And it’s not lost on the 32-year-old that her fans might be equally surprised.

“If you’re familiar with how I am, you know it’s the opposite of what I would have normally done. (I hate to admit),” she continued in the post’s caption. “However this year has been filled with many learning lessons and let’s add this one to the list: how to be okay with being alone.”

The update on the reality star’s personal life comes after revealing that she cheated on Mason—who received the final rose on her unaired season of The Bachelorette—with her ex Mortensen during the very first episode of SLOMW season five. (Paul’s season was ultimately canceled after a 2023 domestic violence video between her and Mortensen surfaced.)

“Obviously we're texting,” Paul said of communicating with Mortensen at the time while in conversation with costars Jessi Draper, Mikayla Matthews and Mayci Neeley. “‘When are you coming home? When are you going to be home?’ I don't know how it led to it, but he came over.”

And after her friends teased her about “not knowing how it happened,” Neely filled in the blank of what occurred next: “You sleep with Dakota."

To which Paul—who at this time was still engaged to Mason—affirmed, “Yes.”

But Paul didn’t exactly see her actions as a betrayal, noting, “I don’t like the word cheating.”

But after receiving some heat for the revelation, the Hulu star—mom to two kids with ex-husband Tate Paul as well as a son with Mortensen—shared she’d be protecting her peace for the foreseeable future.

“Sorry to those that thought they were going to see my redemption arc,” she wrote over a photo of herself on Instagram Sept. 12. “That has slowly just begun. I’ve stayed in, single and celibate this entire time and nobody will have intimate access to me again unless he’s my person and that’s a promise to myself.”

She continued, “Such a long way to go but baby steps.”

Keep reading for a look at where every couple on Mormon Wives stands today…

Taylor Frankie Paul & Dakota Mortensen: Broken Up

While Taylor Frankie Paul's romance with Dakota Mortensen—they welcomed son Ever in 2024—bloomed on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, they called it quits due to Dakota's infidelity.

"Right after Ever was born, Dakota and I were living together and in bliss with our new baby, and I was even considering engagement," Taylor—who began dating the real estate agent in July 2022—revealed during the season two premiere of the Hulu series. "And then I learned that he was lying this entire time."

Taylor was told by a woman named Jenna that she and Dakota had been intimate and he had "spent the night more than once." (He has denied the claims, writing in a September 2024 TikTok that he "never cheated.")

On the series, Taylor said that Dakota accused Jenna of instigating their affair.

"No, it was him," she emphasized in the confessional. "He said he had just kissed her on the couch. No, he went on the couch, they hooked up on the couch, and then they went to the room and they hooked up."

Since ending her romance with the Basin Tiling founder, the mom of three (she shares two kids with ex-husband Tate Paul) was set to find love once again on season 22 of The Bachelorette, but things got a bit thorny when news broke in March 2026 of an alleged confrontation between the exes weeks earlier.

A spokesperson for the Draper City Police Department confirmed to People that there was an open "domestic assault investigation," telling the outlet "allegations have been made in both directions.”

Days later, a video of a previous 2023 physical altercation between Taylor and Dakota surfaced online, prompting ABC to cancel the MomToker's season of the dating franchise.

As for Dakota, he has kicked off a romance with show guest star Shinia Powell, though he previously apologized to Taylor for hooking up with her during a season four episode.

Whitney Leavitt & Connor Leavitt: Married

Whitney Leavitt found the perfect dance partner in Connor Leavitt, whom she wed in 2016. But it wasn't always smooth sailing for the couple—who share kids Sedona, Liam and Billy—as they navigated life in the spotlight.

For instance, the Dancing With the Stars alum, who announced during her Broadway run in May 2026 that she'd be leaving Mormon Wives, had to shut down rumors about her husband's sexuality.

"Do I need to put out a sex tape, or something? Like, trust me," she said on the Off the Vine podcast in October 2024. "We're good. Everything's fine."

"I think it's because when we were going through our personal stuff—and I know you haven't seen it—but he struggled through a porn addiction," she explained. "There's a scene where one of my friends says something along the lines of how they could see how he was confused sexually."

Through the ups and downs, the reality star emphasized that she and Connor—who were 23 and 22, respectively, when they got married—are stronger than ever. In fact, they even renewed their vows in February 2026 for their 10th wedding anniversary.

"We got married really young," Conner told Brides after their ceremony. "It felt like our wedding day, as much as it was for us, it really felt like it was for our families. So we really want to do something to make it ours, and this felt like a really fun way to do it."

Married in 2019, Jen Affleck and Zac Affleck—no relation to Ben Affleck, despite jokes to the contrary—have been at the center of breakup rumors since SLOMW's debut.

In fact, their fight after Jen attended a Chippendales striptease show in Las Vegas became a focal point of the first season. The couple—who share kids Nora, Penelope and Lucas—made up, however, and the Dancing With the Stars contestant later defended their relationship.

"It can be tiring and draining, just because it gets old having to hear the same things," Jen told E! News of the speculations in November 2025. "For me, I'm like, 'People will always talk and people will always have their opinions.' I think it is frustrating for him when people don't see what's happening behind closed doors and how much work and effort he's putting in."

But while Jen announced in June 2026 that she'd be adding to their dance troupe with baby No. 4, the MomToker filed for divorce that November after seven years of marriage.

Jessi Draper & Jordan Ngatikaura: Divorced

Bumps in Jessi Draper and Jordan Ngatikaura's five-year marriage emerged after the hairstylist admitted to having an emotional affair with Vanderpump Villa's Marciano Brunette, though initially it appeared they were working towards smoother roads.

"We are back together," Jessi—who shares kids Jagger and Jovi with Jordan—told E! News in November 2025. "We're trying to work on it. Relationships are not perfect. I think a situation like ours—it's going to take time. It's not going to something that's just amazing overnight."

Sadly, the reconciliation appeared to be short-lived, with Jordan also dad to daughter Peyton from a previous relationship, filing for divorce in March 2026 after five years of marriage.

However, days later, Jessi said she was “blindsided” by his filing and accused him of rushing to submit the paperwork because “he wanted the headline first.”

Admitting that her “heart sunk” seeing the news, she explained, “because we agreed to tell our children together before filing and we haven’t done that.” (E! reached out to attorneys for Jordan for comment but haven’t heard back.)

Though Jessi told E! News that she was "just casually dating and living life," when she brought Marciano as her date to the 2026 American Music Awards in May 2026, he revealed a tattoo dedicated to her that August.

Jessi and Jordan finalized their divorce in September 2026.

Mayci didn't expect to find love with Jacob Neeley. In fact, after the unexpected death of her boyfriend Arik Mack in 2015, when she was just 14 weeks pregnant with their son Hudson, she was prepared to be a single mom.

But it all changed when she met Jacob in 2016 at age 21, whom she would marry two years later.

"After everything I'd been through, I was very guarded, but Jacob was kind and we got on really well," Mayci said in her memoir Told You So. "For a long time, we remained just friends and because we weren't really dating, I was OK with him meeting my son."

"Jacob was amazing with him, which made him appear even more attractive," she continued. "I was terrified of getting hurt again but, after four months, I couldn't deny my feelings any longer. He was kind and funny and made me feel safe."

Mayci and Jacob went on to welcome daughters Harlow in 2021 and Charli in 2025.

Demi Engemann and her husband Bret Engemann tied the knot in 2021, one year after she and Blake Corbin divorced. As the couple's relationship played out on the reality show, their sexual explorations became a major plot point after Whitney gifted Demi a box of Fruity Pebbles.

The truth behind the joke gift wasn't revealed until Jessi shared on Instagram in November 2025 that "grandpa Bret likes to drink her piss like it's dirty soda and he gulps it down like water."

But Demi and Bret aren't crying over spilled secrets—or pee. In fact, she told Entertainment Tonight that December that she and Bret "have nothing else left to do other than own it and have fun with it."

Although their sex life raised eyebrows, the couple has been embracing life with their blended family. While Demi shares daughter Maude with her ex, Bret is dad to his and The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City alum Angie Harrington's sons Rome and Cole.

"I've never seen a dad so involved or love their kids harder, the most devoted step-dad to Maude, and future father to our own children one day," Demi wrote on Instagram in June 2024. "Your ability to remain consistently loyal to your role as father/step-father while navigating all that life throws your way, will never cease to amaze me!"

Mikayla Matthews and Jace Terry have been through it all together. While The reality star first met Jace in 2015 when she was 15 and they welcomed their first son Beckham two years later. Since then, the couple—who tied the knot in 2018—welcomed kids Haven, Tommie and Lottie.

While Mikayla and Jace have been loving life with their four kids, Mikayla admitted that she hopes to grow their family even further.

"When people ask me how many kids I want, I'm like, 'I've always wanted three or four, but I could see myself having six,'" she told People in February 2025. "I'm excited to hopefully move into a new house. I want a big lot for my herd of kids."

However, Mikayla confirmed in the ninth episode of the show's fourth season that she and Jace were taking time apart amid ongoing intimacy struggles.

As Mikayla began unpacking her trauma surrounding years of sexual abuse as a teen, as well as her chronic illness—which causes flare-ups due to heightened stress—their marriage had been deeply affected.

But the tides have officially turned on their connection as the reality star shared during the show's fifth season that she and Jace are back on track.

"I feel like I got a lot more clarity," she said in a confessional on the show, "and so I was able to express more what I needed to Jace."

And, as she added, “He’s been very supportive.”

After Layla Taylor and Clayton Wessel—who are parents to sons Oliver and Maxwell—divorced in 2023, the reality star teased her new romance with Mason McWhorter in July 2025.

Their relationship was a bit complicated on paper. Hang with us: Mason's brother is Chase McWhorter, the ex-husband of Layla's costar Miranda McWhorter. But the pair had been willing to put their romance to the test.

"Right now, I'm kind of scared of marriage but I just want to get to know somebody very well before I even consider that," Layla told Us in November 2025. "I'm just happy and content where me and Mason are. And if somehow that ever were to come up, then we would see."

Unfortunately, the mom of two confirmed that she and Mason had split in February 2026.

"I think we were just on two different paths right now, and he felt in order for him to grow, he had to be on his own," Layla shared. "I respect his decision, and I truly hope that he gets what he wants in life."

As for Layla, who came out as bisexual in June 2026, she soft-launched her romance with a mystery woman a month later in an Instagram video. She later seemed to confirm her relationship with Colorado-based content creator Kelsie Chesser.

Miranda McWhorter & Chase McWhorter: Divorced

Although Miranda is a newer addition to The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, joining in season two, she played a major role in the infamous MomTok "soft swinging scandal." Despite the situation with Taylor, Miranda revealed that drama wasn't the reason for her 2024 divorce from Chase.

"The reasons why we decided to split were things that were issues far before that,” she explained on the Weekly Trash podcast in August 2024. "That might not have helped, for sure, but it definitely did not play a part in the decision process."

Nonetheless, she and Chase have been committed to parenting their kids Brooks and Cohen.

"With co-parenting, you're always having to work on it," she reflected. “The thing is that if we got along perfectly all the time and it was just rainbows and butterflies, we probably wouldn't have gotten divorced."

"The thing with him and I," she continued, "we've always had a pretty good foundation of a friendship prior to even having a romantic relationship. I feel like that's something that set us up for some level of success when it comes to co-parenting."

#832. Kettering Town 'cannot hide' from racism problem

Kettering Town's director of football said the club could no longer hide behind "the comforting lie" that the abuse came from "a small minority"

Non-league Kettering Town have said they "can no longer hide" from the issue of racism after a visiting player was allegedly subjected to "sickening" abuse.

Redditch United player Dan Sweeney said he was targeted by a Kettering supporter during Saturday's Southern League Premier Division Central tie at the Poppies' Latimer Park stadium, which the hosts won 2-1.

The incident comes after a match official reported alleged racial abuse at a Kettering fixture last season, and a previous instance of alleged racist abuse against a Redditch player at Latimer Park in 2017.

In a statement, Kettering director of football Fabian Forde said the "poison" of racism went beyond matchdays.

He also spoke out against the presence of what he called "festering" racism on the club's fans forums.

Writing on the club's website, external, Forde said: "Let's be completely honest with ourselves: this is not the first time. We can no longer hide behind the comforting lie that 'it's just a small minority' or 'they don't reflect the majority of our fans'.

"Every single time we dismiss hate by calling it a minority issue, we minimise the damage. The truth is, if the majority stays silent, that small minority becomes our identity.

"They tarnish our reputation in the eyes of opposition players, fans, and officials. They make our club look like a haven for bigotry. Is that really who we want to be?"

Forde added that the club could not "keep sending out generic statements that mean nothing" and urged fans to support "real cultural change" by taking responsibility for calling out the perpetrators of racist abuse.

He said: "To the majority of our fans, the good, decent people who love this club for the right reasons, we are pleading with you.

"We need you to stand up. We need you to confront this minority head-on. If you see someone typing hate online, call them out. If you hear someone shouting abuse next to you on a Saturday afternoon, don't look away.

"Tell a steward. Identify them to the club. Why are we protecting people who are actively destroying the reputation of the club we love?"

Northamptonshire Police said Saturday's alleged incident had not yet been reported to officers

Northamptonshire Police said they had "not identified any report relating to this [Saturday's] allegation."

However, the force added: "It may be that any report is awaiting allocation or has been made to another police force. Should a report be made elsewhere and the alleged offence be found to have taken place within Northamptonshire, we would take ownership of the investigation.

"We note Kettering Town FC's statement that it is working with its security team, stewards and the relevant authorities to identify those responsible, and we would encourage anyone who believes they have been the victim of a crime to report it to police.

"Racial abuse has no place in football or wider society, and any reports made to us will be assessed and investigated appropriately."

In a statement, external, Redditch United chairman David Faulkner said: "I particularly welcome Kettering Town's commitment to working with its security team, stewards and the relevant authorities to identify those responsible.

"It is vital that this matter is taken seriously and that appropriate action follows.

"Tackling racism requires more than statements. It requires leadership, accountability and a collective willingness to challenge unacceptable behaviour whenever and wherever it occurs.

"We must never allow incidents like this to become normalised, dismissed or simply forgotten once the immediate attention has passed."

The Football Association has also been approached for comment.

#831. Sony Music Publishing Sued Over Stevie Wonder Photo in Album Anniversary Instagram Post

A photographer claims the music publisher used his "iconic" work without a license in a post celebrating 50 years of the album Innervisions.

Sony Music Publishing (SMP) is facing a copyright infringement lawsuit for allegedly posting an “iconic photograph” of Stevie Wonder to its Instagram page without a license.

The Sony Music Group unit was sued on Sunday (Nov. 8) by Alan Satterwhite, a photographer who shot a series of Wonder sitting at a piano in 1974. SMP allegedly included one of those photos in a 2023 Instagram carousel celebrating the 50th anniversary of Wonder’s 1973 album Innervisions, which peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 and spent a total of 89 weeks on the chart.

According to Satterwhite’s lawsuit, obtained and first reported by Billboard, SMP did not buy a license from him before posting the photo to Instagram. He says this alleged infringement “has harmed, and continues to harm, the potential market for or value of the copyrighted work by robbing Plaintiff of his exclusive right to license the copyrighted work for illustrative and other purposes.”

The photographer is now seeking the maximum statutory damages of $150,000 for copyright infringement. An SMP spokesperson declined to comment on the lawsuit.

Satterwhite is no stranger to litigation. He has previously brought more than a dozen lawsuits claiming unauthorized uses of his photos of Wonder and other famous subjects, including Arnold Schwarzenegger and Mel Brooks. Entities sued by Satterwhite have included Amazon, Complex, CBS Radio and the Berklee College of Music.

For its part, SMP usually deals more with the music side of copyright law than the business of image licensing. As the world’s largest music publisher, it often gets pulled into court when songwriters are accused of copying previous works. Such was the case last month, for example, when the owners of Bill Withers’ catalog filed a copyright lawsuit claiming “I’ve Seen It” by SMP breakthrough Olivia Dean mirrored “Just the Two of Us.”

#829. Robbie Williams Defends Olivia Rodrigo Against Plagiarism Claims

Robbie Williams said he "couldn't care less" about fans saying that Olivia Rodrigo's new song "Take Me Home (4 Christmas)" sounds a lot like his 2012 hit "Candy."

No, Robbie Williams doesn't think that Olivia Rodrigo is a traitor.

The "Angels" singer responded to accusations online that Rodrigo's new holiday song "Take Me Home (4 Christmas)" ripped off his 2012 hit "Candy," which he stressed he "couldn't care less" about.

"I love Olivia Rodrigo," Williams said in a statement posted to Instagram Nov. 9. "I've loved her since 'Brutal.' What a f--king record. I wish I'd made it. Also, I cannot believe how much she swears on stage. And that's coming from me. I'm a Sweary Mary, but she's making me look like a Victorian schoolmistress."

"It sounds to me as though she may have accidentally stumbled across a musical echo of mine in one of her new songs," he continued. "And do you know what? I couldn't care less."

The 52-year-old went on to say that he's unsure if the similarities make this "technically a publishing issue, a copyright issue or no issue whatsoever." Either way, he's not interested in finding out.

"I don't want to know," he declared. "I'm not going after her. Because I think at some point, some f--king sanity has to prevail."

The Take That alum hoped to make a broader point in his resistance to taking issue with whatever perceived similarities exist between "Candy" and "Take Me Home," because "artists deserve to be protected."

"There's a difference between protecting your work and treating every vaguely familiar sequence of notes as a winning lottery ticket," Williams explained. "Some of this stuff has become ambulance chasing. And I think it's disgusting."

"We all stand on the shoulders of people who came before us," he added. "Somethings consciously. Sometimes without even knowing it. That's how music works. If we keep punishing people for accidentally arriving somewhere somebody else has already been, eventually we're going to frighten the creativity out of everyone."

Williams concluded his strongly worded statement by sharing a message directed Rodrigo herself.

"Olivia, if you're reading this, I think you're f--king brilliant," he wrote. "But please stop swearing so much. It makes me feel like I have to keep up. And frankly, I'm already swearing far more than necessary."

"Lots of love," Williams finished, "and Happy Christmas. Rob x."

#828. Chelsea staff warned over Fantasy Premier League use

Joao Pedro hasn't played for Chelsea since a win against Everton last month

Chelsea have warned staff to be careful about inadvertently revealing team news through Fantasy Premier League after Joao Pedro's injury appeared to have been disclosed through team selections.

An email was sent to staff reminding them of the potential consequences of using inside information when playing Fantasy Premier League or other public gaming platforms, where team selection choices could reveal which players are unavailable or close to returning.

It followed leaks before the 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham, when Pedro was a surprise absentee because of what has since emerged to be a quad injury.

Several influential Fantasy Premier League content creators claimed to have seen evidence that forward Morgan Rogers, along with several members of Chelsea staff, had removed Pedro from their Fantasy Premier League teams before kick-off at Stamford Bridge, despite no club announcement having been made about his injury.

Asked about the matter by BBC Sport after the defeat, Xabi Alonso said he was unaware of the situation. He replied: "I am not into the fantasy team thing, so I didn't know that."

Since joining Chelsea in the summer, Alonso, 44, has generally been guarded when discussing injury issues in media conferences.

Chelsea have also previously experienced problems with leaks.

During former manager Liam Rosenior's four-month spell in charge last season, team selections were leaked before both legs of the club's Champions League defeat by Paris St-Germain.

It also later emerged former defender Marc Cucurella's barber had revealed on social media that Pedro and Cole Palmer would miss a trip to Brighton last season after discussing the matter with his client.

With regard to Fantasy Premier League, no further restrictions are expected because Chelsea regard the incident as an isolated case that can be managed through greater awareness among players and staff.

There have been many further examples, claiming to suggest players from clubs like Arsenal, Liverpool, Leicester and Newcastle made revealing changes to their teams, while BBC Sport has identified accounts believed by Fantasy Premier League trackers to be linked to high-profile players and figures at clubs across the division.

The highest-profile example was arguably the revelation of then Aston Villa forward Jack Grealish's omission from the squad before a match against Leicester City in February 2021.

Then Leicester manager Brendan Rodgers later said he had been aware of rumours surrounding Grealish's injury absence before the match, which his side won.

More than 11 million people are said to play Fantasy Premier League, which has become an increasingly prominent part of the wider football ecosystem.

Although there are strict rules prohibiting gambling, the Premier League offers no specific guidance to clubs on how, or whether, those involved in the game should participate in Fantasy Premier League.

Instead, it is generally treated as a matter for individual clubs to manage themselves.

#827. AI has transformed maths — this is how we got here

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Anil Ananthaswamy is the author of Why Machines Learn (2024).

Artificial-intelligence tools have found solutions to several mathematics and physics problems that had been unresolved for years. Credit: Barbara Sax/AFP/Getty

Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World Steven Strogatz & Alex Townsend Little, Brown and Company (2026)

When I was studying electrical engineering in India in the 1980s, a professor asked our class: “Why do short- and medium-wave radios produce a crackling sound, or static, when a scooter goes past, regardless of the station you are listening to?” None of us knew the answer.

How AI is reshaping discovery in maths and physics

How AI is reshaping discovery in maths and physics

The professor was using the question to introduce a mathematical operation called a Fourier transform. Each time the spark plug in a scooter engine fires, it produces a short pulse of electromagnetic radiation. The Fourier transform reveals that, mathematically, this signal is a summation of thousands of sine and cosine waves. Whatever frequency our radios are tuned to, the pulse produced by the spark plug contains some energy at that frequency, which we hear as static. It was a proverbial ‘aha’ moment for many of us in the class.

Big Math by mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend contains many such aha moments. But the book is so much more. Strogatz and Townsend use the assuredness of mathematicians and the skill of storytellers to paint a vivid portrait of the variety of ways in which mathematics underpins almost every aspect of people’s lives.

The authors start with an inspiring story about Regina Barzilay, a computer scientist who had breast cancer and, after she finished her treatment in 2014, decided to do something about the lack of tools for spotting the early warning signs of the disease. The technology that she needed to achieve her goal already existed — machine learning — but it was mostly being used to recommend films to people and steer online buying behaviour, and was not reaching many of the people who would benefit from its use in health care. Barzilay collaborated with radiologists and computer scientists to develop a machine-learning model that could predict a person’s risk of developing breast cancer within the next five years from a single mammogram.

The breakthrough proof bringing mathematics closer to a grand unified theor

The breakthrough proof bringing mathematics closer to a grand unified theor

In the book, this story is a set-up for talking about the ubiquitousness of what the authors call ‘big math’ — the mathematics behind technologies that are “shaking the foundations of how we work, how we play, how we learn, how we shop and travel and communicate, even how we heal”.

The authors present the book as more of a conversation than a lecture, but warn that their aim isn’t to make maths “cozy or accessible”. Their disclaimer is welcome and follows in the footsteps of other books published in the past fifteen years that haven’t shied away from getting into the weeds of maths. This includes Strogatz’s own books, The Joy of X (2012) and Infinite Powers (2019), as well as Leonard Susskind’s Theoretical Minimum series on classical and quantum mechanics, and Sean Carroll’s series The Biggest Ideas in the Universe, all of which celebrate the nitty-gritty details of maths to varying degrees.

Saying that, Big Math is light on equations, so the book is more accessible than those mentioned above. But it nevertheless reveals the extent to which maths has permeated people’s lives, for better and for worse.

The seeds of big maths were sown a long time ago. Strogatz and Townsend tell a delightful story about Chinese mathematicians solving accounting problems to estimate the edible rice yield expected from bundles of unprocessed rice still in the husk. The authors neatly pivot to explaining that the problem can be expressed in terms of a system of linear equations (in which variables such as x, y and z do not have exponents, and aren’t multiplied by each other), matrices (rectangular arrays of numbers) and vectors (columns of numbers). This puts us squarely in the middle of the type of maths that is central to artificial intelligence; although the Chinese “reckoners” were solving these equations by moving around sticks of bamboo.

The book is suffused with many such historical anecdotes. We learn, for instance, that nineteenth-century mathematician James Joseph Sylvester thought of the matrix (a term that he coined) as a “mother, a generator, an entity that gave birth to other mathematical objects”. This feels eerily prescient, because the manipulation of massive matrices (with hundreds of billions and even trillions of numbers) is at the heart of generative AI.

How to prevent AI from harming mathematics

How to prevent AI from harming mathematics

They also discuss Leon Festinger’s 1949 idea that repeated matrix–vector multiplications (the kind used to solve the paddy problem) can uncover “hidden structures in social networks”. Over subsequent decades, such matrix methods became key to analysing webs of social relationships to “measure influence, detect clusters, and rank individuals by how connected they were”.

The authors also touch on how the board game of Snakes and Ladders can be used to understand a Markov chain, a mathematical formulation that was key to technology company Google’s early search algorithms. In the game, your next move depends only on your current position and the roll of a die. In maths, a Markov chain is a sequence of random events in which the probability of the next state depends only on the current state and not on any previous one.

Another historical anecdote covered in the book is that of George Dantzig, who, as a graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1939, arrived late to a statistics class and saw two equations written on the blackboard. Thinking that they were homework assignments, he wrote them down. He eventually solved them, but apologized to his professor for taking a few days to do so. The equations, however, were open, unsolved problems. (The legendary mathematician’s story made it into the 1997 film Good Will Hunting, in which actor Matt Damon’s character, Will Hunting, solves a problem scrawled on a blackboard while working as a janitor at a university.)

#826. Bronze named in World 11 for record ninth time

Fifpro has invited players to vote for the Women's World 11 since 2015

England defender Lucy Bronze has been named in the Fifpro Women's World 11 for a record ninth time.

Bronze is one of five England players named, with Alex Greenwood, Alessia Russo, Ella Toone and Hannah Hampton also selected.

Spain defender Irene Paredes also features for the first time since her previous selection in 2017.

Zambia striker Barbra Banda, named in the team for the third time, is the only player in the side based outside England or Spain.

The World 11 - the only global football award chosen exclusively by players - was selected through votes from 6,511 female players from 64 countries.

Goalkeeper: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea, England).

Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea, England), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City, England), Mapi Leon (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Irene Paredes (Barcelona, Spain).

Midfielders: Aitana Bonmati (Barcelona, Spain), Alexia Putellas (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Ella Toone (Manchester United, England)

Forwards: Barbra Banda (Orlando Pride, Zambia), Claudia Pina (Barcelona, Spain), Alessia Russo (Arsenal, England)

Professional players voted based on performances between 4 August 2025 and 16 August 2026, with only those with at least 20 appearances eligible.

Voters were asked to choose the three players who had performed best in each position: goalkeeper, defender, midfielder and forward.

The goalkeeper, three defenders, three midfielders and three forwards who received the most votes were selected for the World 11.

The final place was awarded to the outfield player with the next highest overall vote total, regardless of position.

#824. ROSÉ of BLACKPINK Covers ‘One of My Favorite Songs’ by The Killers at Star-Studded LACMA Gala

The star also played three of her own tracks, including solo release "New Trick."

ROSÉ got out of the APT. on Saturday (Nov. 7), attending the 2026 LACMA Art+Film Gala to perform four songs — including a cover of The Killers — and enjoy a star-studded evening celebrating Dune director Denis Villeneuve and artist Vija Celmins.

As captured in clips from the night, the BLACKPINK star rocked out to “Read My Mind” from the Brandon Flowers-fronted band’s 2006 Billboard 200 No. 2 album Sam’s Town, her live vocals sounding more powerful than ever as she let the emotion of the lyrics lead the way. “This next song is one of my favorite songs to cover,” she said before the tune. “Please sing along if you know it.”

The Los Angeles County Museum of Art also shared a video snippet of ROSÉ jumping up and down and whipping her hair while energetically singing “New Trick,” her new solo song released in September. Dressed in a dainty white dress with a pale pink flower decal on the shoulder, the K-pop superstar also played 12-week Billboard Global 200-topping Bruno Mars duet “APT.” as well as “Number One Girl” from her 2024 debut solo album, Rosie, according to Vanity Fair.

ROSÉ’s mini-concert was for a high-profile audience, with Hollywood elites including Nicole Kidman, Timothée Chalamet, Anya Taylor-Joy, Monica Barbaro, Salma Hayek, Kim Kardashian, Sarah Paulson, Kylie Jenner and more attending the 2026 event. This year, the gala raised a record-breaking sum of nearly $7 million for the museum’s programming.

#821. Alisson wants to sign new Liverpool contract

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker wants to stay at the club beyond the end of the season, when his current contract expires.

The 34-year-old joined from Roma for Â£66.8m in 2018 and has made 347 appearances for the Reds.

"Yes [I want to stay], in my mind. I'm focused on playing every game but in my mind I'm happy to stay," said Alisson.

"That depends on a lot of aspects and different situations. But my will is to stay - I'm happy here and my family is happy here.

"I'm still hungry for titles and to delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can, so that's my thinking."

Last week, Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said he did not know if this would be Alisson's last season at the club but hoped the goalkeeper could "continue for more time".

Asked if he has had conversations over a new deal, Alisson said: "No, but my agent is talking with the club."

The Brazil keeper did consider a move to Juventus earlier this year but ultimately chose to stay at Anfield.

After a difficult week - with Liverpool losing to Arsenal and then Fenerbahce - Alisson made a number of crucial saves in Sunday's win at Crystal Palace.

The goalkeeper says Liverpool now need to find consistency in order to challenge for silverware.

"Our reality is that we're not doing as well as we can. It doesn't mean that we are not doing well - we are doing well in so many games - but the consistency is not there yet," he said.

"We have a top manager, top players. We are capable of great things but as a team we need to get to a point where we feel: 'We are OK now. We have the confidence. We have everything that's needed to win.'

"We are building that. I hope we get there really quick but it takes time.

"We have to be patient but as players, in our mind, we don't have time to waste."

What can you read into Premier League table after 10 games?

Liverpool win at Palace to pile pressure on Sage

This is the first time Alisson has discussed his contract situation this season and, judging by the way he spoke after a superb performance at Selhurst Park, there is a clear desire on his part to stay at Liverpool.

Giorgi Mamardashvili, 26, is waiting in the wings, while highly rated 18-year-old Lucca Brughmans will move to Liverpool from Genk in the summer, so Iraola's side will not be short of goalkeeping options - but it would be a huge call if they do allow Alisson to leave on a free transfer.

His distribution has not been up to the standard we are used to in recent weeks, and that was ruthlessly punished against Arsenal, but the string of saves he made against Palace were a timely reminder that he is still a world-class goalkeeper.

This season, Liverpool have kept four clean sheets in 10 Premier League games but have conceded 10 goals in four Champions League matches, with Alisson playing every minute in both competitions so far.

He is still a leader within the side and was named as one of Iraola's vice-captains at the start of the season.

Alisson did assess his options last season but with senior figures like Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson leaving, he opted to proceed with a one-year extension.

With Virgil van Dijk's contract also set to expire at the end of the season, sporting director Julian Ward has two very important decisions to make when it comes to the future of two men who have been a constant for Liverpool since 2018.

Of course, both command hefty wages, but this is a young Liverpool side trying to find their way under Iraola - and the head coach will be aware of the importance of two experienced players who have been with the club for such a long time.

Perhaps a one-year extension can be offered to Alisson which could allow Brughmans to learn from the Brazilian but, at 34, he may be looking for the security of something longer term.

Either way, Liverpool's hierarchy will have a keen eye on how Alisson fares as the season progresses. If he can carry on performing like he did against Palace, then a new contract will be a no-brainer.

#818. 15 Great Songs That Use the Wah-Wah Guitar Pedal & Its Funky, Fluid Feel

Del Casher, the inventor of the wah-wah pedal, died last month at 88. His creation has had a massive impact on musical history.

This week, the family of session musician and Gene Autry and Frank Sinatra collaborator Del Casher announced that he had died on Oct. 1 at the age of 88. But Casher was not just a musician who played on several records with iconic artists: he was also the inventor of the wah-wah pedal, one of the most significant technical innovations in electric guitar history.

, who had created the pedal and its instantly-recognizable tone shifter, showed off the pedal to Frank Zappa during a jam session with the Mothers of Invention in 1966; Zappa subsequently gave one to Jimi Hendrix, who made it the centerpiece of his guitar virtuosity across his short but wildly influential career. And Hendrix was hardly alone. From the late 1960s onward, hundreds, if not thousands, of rock guitarists utilized the pedal, either to craft distinctive riffs or to enhance and distort their solos, creating some of the most iconic recordings in recorded music history along the way.

And lest anyone think the pedal’s use was limited to the classic rock set, it’s been used across a wide variety of different genres, from blues to funk to soul to heavy metal to hip-hop to hair metal to jam bands to grunge, and just about everything in between, with guitarists such as Eric Clapton, Jimmy Page, Eddie Hazel, Trey Anastasio, Jerry Cantrell, Kirk Hammett, Mike McCready and so many more all using it to twist and turn their tone around. (Famed Motown guitarist Melvin Ragin even earned the nickname “Wah Wah Watson” for — well, you can work that out.)

In honor of Casher’s death and the impact his great invention had, here are 15 great songs that utilized the wah-wah pedal over the years.

Of all of Hendrix’s songs on which he used his wah, “Voodoo Child” is the most iconic, simply for the introduction — probably the single most high-profile use of the pedal in music history.

Shortly after Hendrix made his grand statement, Eric Clapton — still in his supergroup era before embarking on his solo career — fell in love with the pedal, using it on several classic tracks across Cream’s discography. None stands out as boldly as “White Room,” with its swaggering solo grandstanding its way towards the song’s fade-out finale.

The wah swept its way through all of that era’s iconic guitarists — but rather than use it to push his guitar sound to the absolute limit within his solos, Led Zeppelin guitarist Jimmy Page took it to a creepy and haunting place. Page used its tone shimmering effect to create atmosphere on “Dazed and Confused” that almost sounded like a banshee wail at times. And this was separate from what he wound up getting into once he started messing around with theremins.

Just over a minute into this snarling, driving track off 1969’s Hot Rats, Zappa starts to go off, leaning into the weird and wiggly side of what a wah can produce — and then he doesn’t really stop for the proceeding eight-plus minutes, exploring up and down his fretboard and stretching what started as a tight band turning the screws into a sprawling adventure that weaves in and out of coherence but manages to stay locked in with his rhythm section all the same. It’s an exercise in the pedal’s versatility, to some degree; to another degree, it’s a mad scientist at work with his tools, following wherever they take him.

The wah sound here came from the aforementioned Wah Wah Watson, who joined the Motown house band the Funk Brothers in 1968 and brought his favored pedal into the legendary Detroit studio and onto its classic records. The Temptations track is defined by Watson’s slippery, almost juicy-wet wah chording, bringing the wah out of the realm of the solo and into the backbone of the song.

Is there a more iconic opening triplet than the wah-wah’d notes that open this Marvin Gaye classic? The very thought of it turns the romance of a room right up, and even though the wah doesn’t play much of a further role in the song — Gaye’s voice, as well as the horn and rhythm sections, really take over — it’s a statement of an opening. Commonly thought to be another Wah Wah Watson lick — he did play on the track — some say it was actually played on the record by Don Peake, a Motown session man. It’s unclear who actually it is on the record itself.

There is so much about a wah pedal that informs various aspects of funk that it’s almost hard to keep track of it all — and you could argue that the wah here isn’t even the funkiest part of the song, or even the most essential piece of guitar work on it. (The metronomic rhythm guitar has as much to do with the feel.) But it’s another example of how it wormed its way into that particular art form given its wobbly affect — perfect for shaking the booty. Much like Curtis Mayfield’s “Freddie’s Dead,” the wah guitar is secondary here, though no less essential.

Funkadelic is one of the great funk bands of all time, being, alongside its sister act Parliament, the brainchild of Dr. Funkenstein himself George Clinton. But this track, one of Funkadelic’s most enduring, isn’t much of a funk song at all. Instead, it’s a clear-out showcase for guitarist Eddie Hazel, who was told — while on acid in the studio, as the story goes — to imagine that his mother had died; the result is him using the wah pedal to almost literally make his guitar sound like it was weeping for the better part of 10 minutes, one of the most emotional uses of the pedal in history.

Chicago is known for a lot of things, but this one is probably the band’s most famous song — and one of its most famous elements is the extended solo by lead guitarist Terry Kath, which starts off with a distorted rampage and then halfway through shifts into a wah-fevered whirling dervish as Kath climbs the fretboard. It stands out for its tone, and how much the pedal warps his guitar when he steps on it, showcasing clearly how its effect can border on the delirious.

Most might remember the shimmering keys or soaring strings being the standout from the “Shaft” theme song, but it’s the splashy wah that truly drives the song along in the undercurrent. It gave the groove that fluid feel that helped to define the track — and to propel it to No. 1 on the Hot 100, as well as to an Academy Award for best original song. That’d be the work of Charles “Skip” Pitts, who also worked with the Isley Brothers and as a Stax studio man, ultimately getting sampled left and right once hip-hop came along.

There are several different iconic guitar tones on this Metallica classic — and this is far from the only one of their songs where Kirk Hammett uses it — but the wah, first in the background during the signature riff, then as the rocket fuel for Hammett’s solo, is the star of the show. It turns his notes into a primal shriek that is as effective as nightmare fuel as James Hetfield’s vocals or Lars Ulrich’s unforgiving drums.

The riff that did more than anything else to turn Slash into a guitar god is a masterpiece in and of itself, and we mean to take nothing away from it. But his “Sweet Child O’ Mine” guitar solo is almost as famous, depending on who you talk to, and its sing-song lyrical quality comes not just through his flawless tone — a perfect meld of his hands and his Les Paul — but the wah on which he rocks when he kicks things into overdrove halfway through. It’s perfect Slash: always in control, yet seemingly always teetering on the edge of excess. Come to think of it, that encapsulates much of Guns N’ Roses’ first records, too.

The wah is often associated with funk, dance, wobble and overdriven solos — but Jerry Cantrell took it to another place entirely on Alice in Chains’ breakthrough hit “Man in the Box.” In his hands, it becomes a monster, distorting his guitar into a stomping, chomping machine with sinister intentions during the heavy riffing on the song’s verses, and then into cries of pain and agony on his subsequent solo. It’s a guitar sound that immediately contorts the face into a scowl, and the vocal-doubling effects he uses to echo Layne Staley’s voice gives it an extra heaviness that makes it extra evocative.

It is funny to think that Pearl Jam and Alice In Chains are often grouped together, since outside of both being from Seattle the two bands ultimately had very little in common. But one thing that Alice guitarist Cantrell and PJ lead Mike McCready always shared was an enduring love for the wah pedal, and on this track, off Pearl Jam’s sophomore album Vs., is McCready at his most unhinged, using his wah pedal on a solo that goes beyond all concept of actual notes and pushes into almost pure emotion — like a runaway train, or a guttural scream in guitar form, elevating Eddie Vedder’s vocals into the stratosphere.

Take your pick of Phish live, of course, because Trey Anastasio always brings out his wah pedal when it’s time to get into the funk no matter what actual song the band is playing — or indeed if they’re playing any recognizable song at all. But very few Phish songs are as defined by his staccato wah style as “The Moma Dance,” a fan favorite that often is used as the launchpad for a full-arena dance party, and that, of course, goes much harder in a live setting. Trey often uses his wah to enhance his solos — “Farmhouse” and “Ghost” are notable examples off the top — but “Moma” is one that is based upon this slippery groove that makes it impossible to stand still.

#817. Burn replaces injured Guehi in England squad

Dan Burn and Marc Guehi were both part of England's 2026 World Cup squad

Newcastle's Dan Burn has been added to the England squad to play Croatia and Spain in the Nations League this week after Manchester City defender Marc Guehi pulled out with a hip injury.

Guehi was substituted at half-time of City's loss at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and manager Enzo Maresca said afterwards the centre-back had requested to come off because of the injury.

BBC Sport revealed on Sunday that the 26-year-old was having a scan to determine the severity of the ongoing issue, and the defender has now been ruled out of this week's matches.

The former Crystal Palace captain has been a mainstay of Thomas Tuchel's team since his appointment as England head coach in January 2025.

Guehi started in all but one of England's games at the World Cup and all four of the team's Nations League fixtures in September and October.

Burn has 11 international caps and was also part of Tuchel's squad for the World Cup, where he made two substitute appearances.

The 34-year-old has not featured for the Three Lions since after he missed the previous international break with an ankle injury.

England face Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, before travelling to Madrid to face World Cup winners Spain on Saturday.

#816. Dax Shepard Reacts to Claims His, Kristen Bell's Marriage Is "Abusive"

Dax Shepard shut down speculation that he is "controlling" and "abusive" toward his wife Kristen Bell, describing the accusations on Nov. 9's Armchair Expert as "a level of unjustness."

Dax Shepard is setting the record straight.

Two weeks after Kristen Bell shared that her husband flirts with her by complimenting their waiter or waitress while on a date, the Parenthood actor addressed misconceptions about their 13-year-old marriage.

"Another round of me being a terrible person was in the media, and I avoided that," Shepard began on the Nov. 9 episode of his Armchair Expert podcast. "But then it hit Kristen's doorstep really hard, and then I got to find out everything that people are saying about me."

He argued that there is "a level of unjustness" regarding the perception of his behavior, noting that there is "this weird narrative that is surrounding me as controlling, abusive, now flirting with people in public, which I don't do."

The 51-year-old acknowledged that the way Bell—with whom he shares two daughters—explained their dynamic on the Oct. 26 episode of his podcast alongside her Nobody Wants This costars could have been misconstrued.

"I think she phrased it in a way that got intentionally, easily confused for people because we're saying I flirt with Kristen by tipping people a lot and I flirt with Kristen by complimenting people," Shepard said, "If you think I'm complimenting hot young waitresses, you got a problem."

"I'm finding the dude that I don't think has had a compliment in a while and tell him I love his shoes," he clarified. "It's always somebody that I want to make their day. So those compliments are flirting with Kristen. But it got to be, when it went through the grinder, that I flirt with people in front of Kristen."

The podcast host also shut down speculations that he abuses his wife or their kids.

"For me, growing up around certain men who behaved a certain way, and then literally dedicating my whole life to being the opposite of all that," he shared, "I don't ever yell at my children. I don't swear at them. I don't yell at my wife. To have given it my all to be the opposite of what, now, some group of people is saying I am is hard."

"I find it deeply insulting to my wife, additionally," Shepard continued. "She's what? She's sitting in a house with her two daughters and modeling some abusive relationship? It's very offensive to her."

Bell explained during the previous episode that she feels her husband is flirting with her by complimenting others and making them feel good.

"If we go to a dinner or something, there's a couple things Dax does where he doesn't have to look up and wink at me, but I know that he's just being the best boy," she recalled. "We'll be at dinner and he'll say to the waiter, waitress, he'll go, 'Wow, you have incredible eyelashes, gorgeous eyes, great job.'"

The Frozen star's heart totally melts when Shepard "actively smiles at people and gives them compliments."

As Bell and Shepard try their best to tune out the critics, keep reading for a look back at their sweet romance.

Dax Shepard shared a kiss with daughters Lincoln and Delta, who were dressed in chic French-style ensembles that included striped tees and berets. Kristen Bell captioned the post in honor of her husband's birthday in January 2025, "I cannot imagine life without you."

Kristen had a rosy time going "flower farming" with her girls during a trip to S.E. Daugherty & Sons Farms in Nashville, Tenn., in July 2025.

Delta and Lincoln took in the sunset view with their furry friend in summer 2025. As Kristen put it in her Instagram post, "Lake life : 5 out of 5 jalapeños."

The Parenthood alum gave a kiss to his daughter while out to dinner.

Kristen provided a glimpse at their family bond while honoring Dax's sobriety anniversary in September 2025.

"This is what 21 years of sobriety looks like," she wrote. "Lots of hugging. Hugging everyone and everything. Hugging life. Thank you for getting sober, @daxshepard. I am eternally grateful to have you. We all are."

The father-daughter duo cuddled during a sweet moment in another snap.

The family got emotional while sharing an embrace at school.

Dax proved he's the ultimate girl dad while sharing a hug with his kiddo, clan in lemon pajamas.

When his daughter got too tired on a boat outing, Dax carried her on his lap as he sat at the wheel.

#815. Aberdeen sack Robinson after league slump

Robinson's final interview as Aberdeen boss

Stephen Robinson's Aberdeen reign is over inside eight months, with the head coach sacked after winning just three from 12 Premiership matches this season.

The Dons sit second bottom and Saturday's 4-0 home defeat by Hibernian was their fourth straight loss in all competitions.

Brian Kerr and Stephen Craigan have also left the club, with Stuart Duff placed in interim charge.

Club hero Willie Miller described Saturday's result as "utterly embarrassing", going on to tell BBC Sportsound listeners that Robinson resembled "a man lost".

The 51-year-old former Northern Ireland international previously managed Oldham Athletic, Motherwell, Morecambe and St Mirren.

On the back of three successive top-six finishes and a League Cup triumph, Robinson left the Paisley side for Aberdeen in March, agreeing a contract until the summer of 2029.

The sixth permanent manager since Dave Cormack took control at Pittodrie in November 2019, he steered the Dons away from relegation trouble last term before overhauling the squad with 15 signings.

Across 28 games in all competitions, Robinson departs with a record of 11 wins, five draws and 12 defeats.

'Aberdeen hunt yet another manager after ill-fated Robinson reign'

The next manager will inherit a squad low on confidence, the joint lowest scorers in the league.

Robinson chopped and changed between four and five at the back but that yielded just two top-flight clean sheets.

Of the plethora of summer recruits, only goalkeeper Marius Muller and full-back Nesta Guinness-Walker have played in every league game.

Top scorer Kevin Nisbet is the other player to have done the same and scunnered fans cheered when the captain was replaced at the weekend.

"The players aren't up to scratch, not up to playing at this level and dealing with high-ish expectations," was the damning assessment from Miller.

"I'm not talking about trophies, I'm talking about being in the top six and they're nowhere near that."

After the international break, Aberdeen travel to face Kilmarnock on 21 November then visit Rangers three days later before their next home game against Dundee on 28 November.

Halliday questions Aberdeen players after 'giving up' on Robinson

Former Aberdeen captain, manager & director Willie Miller

You are looking at 15 payers out and 15 players in, so it is a huge turnaround of players, was that all Stephen Robinson? I would imagine probably yes but I don't know because I am not privy to that information.

But at the same time, when you make that amount of changes, when you have assessed the squad and to be fair on Stephen as well he came in at a very uncertain time and relegation perhaps staring the club in the face so he managed initially to get the performances with the players he inherited.

But then you make all the changes with the support from the board, you bring all these new players in and I think there was never a stable formation either.

The board have really worked hard over the years to try and get Aberdeen back to a kind of level, won a cup a couple of years ago. I don't blame the board for anything at all.

Recruitment is absolutely key and if you've bought a bunch of players and then they're not performing then that is a real worry. There's a few players in there that are already at a good level but can the others jump on that wagon and get Aberdeen rolling again because it's a very difficult time for them.

I'm not going to criticise the players because I'm not really sure what level they're at. You have to be a fairly good level to be in the Aberdeen team and to get back to that kind of level is going to be tough.

The phrase rinse and repeat may apply to hair washing, but these days it also applies to Aberdeen's recruitment of managers.

While no-one can fault the commitment chairman Dave Cormack has shown to the club during his tenure, the managerial success rate under his stewardship is low - and that is probably putting a positive spin on things.

For the Dons, this procedure feels like a movie that has had a number of disappointing sequels.

Barring last year's Scottish Cup win, there has been a general downward trajectory in fortunes for Aberdeen. Undoubtedly, the constant chopping and changing has been a huge factor.

As for Robinson - it felt like he has been swimming against the North Sea tide since his appointment.

He came in after a protracted search to find Jimmy Thelin's successor and his appointment was not greeted with much approval from the Red Army, who viewed it as one driven more by panic than anything else.

The frustration and disgruntlement among the Aberdeen support has only grown, one which has certainly felt like it has long gone past any tipping point.

Robinson has cut a beleaguered figure in the dugout, and post-match interviews during the dying embers of his tenure were difficult.

Now it is over to recently appointed chief executive Adrian Bevington.

Much has been made of the network of contacts both Bevington and sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel possess.

Those will be needed as they aim to make an appointment whose first priority will be to stop an alarming slide that is threatening to plunge them in to the darkest of relegation mires.

#814. Toukie Smith—Model, Actress and Robert De Niro's Ex—Dead at 74

Toukie Smith, a model and 227 star who also shared two kids with ex Robert De Niro, died Nov. 4, her and De Niro’s children confirmed in a statement. She was 74.

A model has left the world after making a tremendous impact.

Toukie Smith, a model who was also known for her role as Eva Rawley in 227, died Nov. 4 after a “long, courageous battle” with multiple sclerosis, her and ex Robert De Niro’s children Airyn and Julian confirmed to The Hollywood Reporter. She was 74.

Smith, born Doris A. Smith, was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania in 1952 and made her debut in the modeling industry in the 1970s, inspired by her brother Willi Smith, a renowned fashion designer and often used her as his muse.

In 1989, she scored the role as Eva on the final seasons of the NBC sitcom that also starred Regina King, Marla Gibbs and Helen Martin. She went on to appear in Joe’s Apartment, Miami Vice and Goosed but later admitted it was hard for her to break through in Hollywood.

"Everybody has to get it right," she told the New York Times in 1992. "I am an actress first. I'm not a sometime model.”

Nevertheless, she joked, “I thought modeling was rough with rejection. Huh! Welcome to the real world of acting!”

But Smith’s life couldn’t simply be narrowed down into one career. In addition to acting as well as appearing in modeling campaigns for Chanel, Versace and Yves Saint Laurent, she also opened a restaurant, Toukie’s, in 1994. The establishment sat on West Houston in Manhattan and donated some of its profits to help those fighting AIDs in honor of her brother, who died from illness related to the disease in 1987.

“I opened this place because big parties are one thing,” she told the New York Times after the restaurant opened, “but now it's time for us to come together, to connect.”

Smith and De Niro—who began dating in 1988—welcomed Airyn and Julian in 1995 through a surrogate. The former couple split about a year later, but while they often stepped out together, they rarely shared more insight into their romance. As she told the Los Angeles Times when asked about the romance in 1990, “What’s great about a private life is it’s private.”

What Smith was most known for, however, is synonymous with her nickname, which she said her grandmother gave her from a children’s song about a determined fire engine.

As she told the Los Angeles Times of the moniker, “I’ve always had lots of energy.”

For a deeper look at De Niro’s family tree, keep reading…

Robert De Niro met his first wife, Diahnne Abbott, while making Martin Scorsese's Taxi Driver, in which she had a bit part as the ticket taker at a porn theater Travis Bickle patronizes in the gritty 1976 classic.

The couple also appeared together in Scorsese's 1977 tortured-romance drama New York, New York and his 1982 satire The King of Comedy.

The actor adopted Diahnne's daughter Drena, born Sept. 3, 1967, when they got married.

Drena's first Instagram post is a black-and-white snap of her as a child out to dinner with her parents and then-couple Jack Nicholson and Anjelica Huston, captioned "At this point all I wonder is WTF was I doing there ???"

She caught the creative bug early, though, and remained in show business as an actor and producer.

Growing up, "it definitely wasn't the typical family lifestyle," she told Everything Zoomer, "but there was a lot of warmth, fun, craziness." She described her father as "a non-judgmental, open-minded person, always accepting of what people feel their paths are."

De Niro and Abbott's son Raphael De Niro was born Nov. 9, 1976.

Raphael later recalled the family moving from Los Angeles (where his father was born) to New York (the city De Niro is most associated with) when he was about 10, telling The Real Deal it was a major "culture shock."

Raphael went into real estate, which also runs in the family. Per his website, he leads The De Niro Team at Douglas Elliman in Manhattan, and he's a partner in TriBeCa's Greenwich Hotel.

He shares three kids with ex-wife Claudine de Matos and has been married to stylist Hannah Carnes since March 2020.

Acknowledging his last name alone turned him into fodder for tabloid coverage, Raphael told The Real Deal, "I just try to keep my head down and keep my private life private."

Leandro De Niro Rodriguez, Drena's son with artist ex Carlos Rodriguez, died of a suspected overdose on July 2, 2023. He was 19.

On Aug. 11, 2023, which would have been her son's 20th birthday, Drena wrote on Instagram, "Thank you for the happiest and most profound 2 decades of my life, little angel. I hope you are at peace and your spirit is filled with joy today and always."

De Niro called his grandson's death a shock, telling People, "And I just then started thinking about all the things I could have, should have done maybe with him. I don't know if that would've made a difference. And so that's always playing through my mind. It shouldn't have happened."

De Niro and model-actress Toukie Smith started dating in 1988, but ended their romantic relationship several years before their twins Julian and Airyn were born via surrogate on Oct. 20, 1995.

The exes would be leading "separate personal and professional lives," De Niro's rep said in a statement at the time, but "look forward to sharing the parenting of the children."

A rep for Smith said, per the New York Times, that the pair "obviously still have a very strong bond."

Airyn came out as a transgender woman in April 2025. She told Them Magazine that her journey also brought her closer to her racial identity.

"I think a big part of [my transition] is the influence Black women have had on me," she said. "I think stepping into this new identity, while also being more proud of my Blackness, makes me feel closer to them in some way."

As for who the actress aspires to be like? Her mother, of course.

"Whenever I'm at a family gathering on my dad's side, people would always talk about how much they love my mom and how memorable she was and how happy my dad was when he was with her," she shared. "I want to be like that… I want to be remembered the way that people remember her."

De Niro signaled that his feelings for his child hadn't changed in any way, saying in a statement, "I loved and supported Aaron as my son and now I love and support Airyn as my daughter. I don't know what the big deal is. I love all my children."

Julian is a stage and screen actor who appeared on Broadway in the Tony-nominated The Sign in Sidney Brustein's Window. In 2022 he played a young Barack Obama in the Showtime limited series The First Lady and appeared on the Netflix series Zero Day, starring his dad as a former POTUS investigating a deadly cyberattack.

"For my kids, I tell them, 'If you want to be an actor or you want to do this or that, that's fine as long as you're happy. Just don't sell yourself short,'" De Niro told People in January 2020. "That's the most I would say—push yourself a little more and reach for what you really think it is you want to do. Don't be afraid."

De Niro married Grace Hightower on June 17, 1997.

The welcomed son Elliot De Niro on March 18, 1998. De Niro filed for divorce from the Precious actress in August 1999, but they reconciled and renewed their vows in 2004.

“They can make sure this one sticks," the actor joked of the two judges who officiated, per People.

In 2009, De Niro, then 66, told the Los Angeles Times, "My whole thing now is just to have the strength to keep my kids in line and get them to the point where they’re independent and self-reliant. I want to make sure my kids know I’m there, and you’ve got to have the stamina to do that.”

Daughter Helen Grace De Niro was born via surrogate on Dec. 23, 2011.

When promoting Silver Linings Playbook, in which he played a father whose grown son (played by Bradley Cooper) has bipolar disorder, De Niro opened up about having a child with special needs.

"I don't like to get emotional," he told Katie Couric in 2013, "but I know exactly what [my character] goes through."

He shared in 2016 that Elliot has autism.

"She's so adorable," De Niro said of his then 1-year-old daughter in 2013. He told CBS News, "You just look at her, and it's all there...Nothing else matters."

Helen made a rare red carpet appearance with her dad and his girlfriend Tiffany Chen at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.

De Niro was first photographed with Chen in August 2021, but his relationship with the tai chi expert wasn't the subject of much notice until after their daughter Gia Virginia Chen-De Niro was born on April 6, 2023.

"This baby was planned," Gayle King relayed in announcing Gia's arrival a month later on CBS Mornings, and "brought here by love."

While De Niro admittedly doesn't do the "heavy lifting," he waxed rhapsodic about having a baby in the house.

"Everything that I'm consumed with or worried about just goes away when I look at her," he told AARP in January 2024. "It's wondrous."

And at 2 years old, Gia continued to be "pure joy," De Niro told Entertainment Tonight in June 2025. "It's always wonderful."

#811. Juan Atkins’ Catalog Surges 1,285% on Streaming After Producer’s Death

The techno founder died on Oct. 31 at age 64.

The catalog of techno founder Juan Atkins has seen a massive streaming surge following the producer’s death on Oct. 31.

Between Oct. 30 and Nov. 5, U.S. streams of Atkins’ catalog went up by 1,285%, according to Luminate. In the week of Oct. 23-29, Atkins’ catalog received 6,000 U.S. on-demand streams; following his death, the number rose to 86,000 U.S. on-demand streams. Similarly, Atkins’ global streams increased by 1,103% the same week.

Two of Atkins’ key side projects also saw significant streaming boosts. In the week of Oct. 30-Nov. 5, Cybotron — composed of Atkins and producer Rik Davis — boasted 84,000 total U.S. on-demand streams. That was up from 26,000 the week prior, representing a 228% increase. Founded in Detroit, Cybotron released its debut album, Enter, in 1983. Its key track, “Clear,” reached No. 52 on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs on Oct. 8, 1983 and was later sampled on Missy Elliott’s Timbaland-produced “Lose Control” in 2005. “Clear” ranked No. 77 on Billboard‘s 2025 list of the 100 Best Dance Songs of All Time.

Meanwhile, streams for Model 500, an Atkins solo alias, were up 492% following his death, rising from 8,000 to 46,000 U.S. on-demand streams week over week.

On Oct. 31, Atkins was found unresponsive in his hotel room in Mexico City before a scheduled performance. He was transported to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead shortly after arriving. No cause of death has been announced.

Atkins is a founder of techno, a genre he co-created alongside Kevin Saunderson and Derrick May as part of The Belleville Three — so-called because the trio initially worked in the Detroit suburb of Belleville. His productions are credited for presenting not only new sounds but new sonic worlds, with fellow techno pioneer Jeff Mills remembering Atkins as being “among a rare and select group of visionary musicians who helped construct a bridge into the 21st century.”

Following his death, Atkins was also fondly remembered by an array of fellow electronic music producers around the world.

#810. Incident-by-incident: Was it a bad weekend for VAR?

Manchester United's last-gasp equaliser against Aston Villa survived a VAR review for a potential foul

Whisper it quietly, but the statistics say video assistant referee decisions have been pretty good in the Premier League so far this season.

The Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel, which looks at every contentious decision and votes whether it is right or wrong, reported just two VAR errors after eight rounds of matches.

At the same stage last season, there had been six mistakes.

Then came this weekend, during which almost every top-flight game had a controversial decision.

BBC Sport looks at most of these situations - there really were too many to do them all - and assesses the likelihood that the KMI Panel will add to the list of errors.

Man Utd grab a point in dramatic fashion late on against Aston Villa

Incident 1: Penalty awarded to Manchester United for a foul by Boubacar Kamara on Matheus Cunha in the 16th minute.

Verdict: The spot-kick was awarded because the Villa defender went through Cunha to win the ball. Replays clearly showed the first contact was on the Brazilian's foot.

What the KMI Panel might say: This will be a correct decision.

Incident 2: Possible foul by Senne Lammens on Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki before Patrick Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser.

Verdict : There are similarities to a goal Arsenal scored at Old Trafford last season, when William Saliba leant into United goalkeeper Altay BayÄ±ndÄ±r.

Lammens was not looking at the ball, which increases the chances of a VAR intervention.

What the KMI Panel might say: With the higher bar for an intervention in the Premier League, and minimal contact, it is unlikely to be a VAR error to not disallow the goal.

Why Arsenal should have been given a penalty against Hull

Incident: Kai Havertz was pulled down inside the area by Nobel Mendy. The VAR, Michael Oliver, sent referee Farai Hallam to the pitchside monitor for a penalty, but it was not given due to an offside offence by the Germany international.

Verdict: BBC Sport covered this incident in detail on Saturday. As the foul happened before any potential offside offence, the penalty should have been awarded.

What the KMI Panel might say: Even though it feels wrong to reward a player in an offside position with a penalty, the law says otherwise and this is likely to be a mistake.

Should Bogle have seen red for this challenge in the Leeds v Tottenham game?

Incident: Jayden Bogle fouled Mathys Tel, with referee John Brooks giving the free-kick but no sanction for the Leeds player. The VAR, Tony Harrington, opted not to send Brooks to the monitor for a red card.

Verdict: BBC Sport covered the merits of this incident on Saturday. It was a difficult call for the VAR, because Bogle caused the foul with his supporting rather than his challenging foot. Still, it was a very painful challenge and some believe it should have been a red card.

What the KMI Panel might say: Was it an unfortunate incident, or a tackle which endangered the opponent? This will depend upon which former players are on the KMI Panel for this week, because it has split opinion among ex-pros.

Frank Lampard post-match interview - Everton v Coventry

All three incidents were covered in more detail by BBC Sport on Friday.

Incident 1: Coventry's Caleb Yirenkyi appeared to have his hair pulled inside the area by James Tarkowski, but no penalty was awarded.

Verdict: While the interpretation on hair pulling was relaxed for this season, meaning this would not be a red card, there appeared to be a yank of the hair by the Everton defender.

What the KMI Panel might say: Incorrect decision, penalty kick.

Incident 2: Another penalty claim for Coventry as Everton's Vitalii Mykolenko clipped Taiwo Awoniyi on the edge of the box.

Verdict: Replays shows that the contact on Awoniyi was made just before the line.

What the KMI Panel might say: Correct decision, no penalty.

Incident 3: Thierno Barry put Everton in front in the 61st minute, but there was a VAR check for a potential handball.

Verdict: The VAR determined there was no conclusive evidence for a handball, yet there does appear to be a deviation and the goal probably should have been ruled out.

What the KMI Panel might say: As the VAR does not have the super-zoom - this takes a few minutes to calibrate and is not available instantly - no VAR intervention might be supported. This was the case with a goal scored by Crystal Palace against Nottingham Forest. It could be a split vote.

Igor Thiago will be suspended for three Premier League games after his VAR red card for violent conduct

Incident: Igor Thiago was sent off following a VAR review after he caught the head of Chema Andres with his forearm.

Verdict: The Brentford striker can consider himself unfortunate, as there is doubt that he truly intended to catch the Spaniard in the face.

What the KMI Panel might say: It may seem like a soft dismissal, but the VAR intervention is likely to be supported because the law does say that a strike to the head should be a red card, unless force is negligible.

'Yellow card for me' - Dublin on Thiago red card

Incident: Crystal Palace were awarded a penalty three minutes into stoppage time for a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio.

Verdict: We saw a similar incident the 2024-25 season when Arsenal defender William Saliba headed Joao Pedro after the Brighton striker had won the ball. This was voted to be a correct penalty decision.

What the KMI Panel might say: This incident is not quite the same as Saliba on Pedro, and more of a 50-50 clash. It may be voted as an on-field error, but not to the threshold for VAR.

Incident: Cole Palmer went down on the edge of the area under a challenge from both Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka, and asked for a penalty. Referee Jarred Gillett did not give a foul.

Verdict: A foul is determined by the first contact on the attacker. That a player falls into the box with contact continuing would not make it a penalty. Only on holding offences is continuing contact relevant.

What the KMI Panel might say: There is no conclusive evidence that any initial foul contact happened inside the area, so no penalty is likely to be supported.

Incident: Newcastle thought they had taken the lead at Craven Cottage, only for the goal to be ruled out for a foul by Yoane Wissa on Timothy Castagne.

Verdict: Matthias Jaissle was perplexed in his post-match interview, yet he would surely be furious if a Fulham player held one of his defenders back to create on onside corridor for another attacker to score.

What the KMI Panel might say: This is likely to be voted as a correct decision.

BBC Sport estimates that there are two decisions which the KMI Panel is very likely to log as a VAR error: not awarding penalties to Arsenal and Coventry.

Two further calls, Barry's goal and the potential red card to Bogle, may be errors but will depend who is on the panel and where their subjective opinion lies.

The others on the list are likely to be correct.

So we are potentially looking at two to four errors, which is not a good weekend.
